topic: Adaptive root-N inference through a vanishing spatial-confounding cross-tail. For d in {1,2}, observe X(s_i) and Y(s_i)=beta X(s_i)+W(s_i) on deterministic quasi-uniform designs in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain, with fill distance comparable to N^(-1/d), separation comparable to fill distance, and bounded local-stencil degree. Let (X,W) be a centered stationary bivariate Gaussian field with Matérn marginal smoothness one-half, compact positive scales and ranges, and cross-spectrum A(alpha_C^2+||omega||^2)^(-(p+d/2)), where p lies in a fixed compact subinterval of (1/2,1), A may have either sign or vanish, and the spectral determinant has a fixed positive margin. Construct three or more nested affine-annihilating local-stencil slope statistics and a finite-dimensional profile confidence set for beta over the observation-scale tail amplitude and p. Prove a uniform actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, asymptotic 1-alpha coverage through every sequence A_N->0, O(N^(-1/2)) worst-case expected diameter and squared-risk O(N^(-1)), plus a matching honest-length lower bound. Explicitly control boundary, aliasing, irregular-design, denominator and Matérn remainder terms; do not assume independent Fourier coordinates, known p, efficient constants, unknown marginal smoothness adaptation, or a broader covariance class. Use Burman-Ogburn-Datta's PM2.5/COVID county-centroid homogeneous slope as the conditional applied consumer when the Matérn and design diagnostics hold. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Three scales have the exact annihilator (tu,-t-u,1), orthogonal to both power-law nuisance directions v(t)=(1,t,t^2) and v(u), while its inner product with the slope direction is (t-1)(u-1); compact p-bounds therefore separate beta uniformly even when amplitude is zero. Reparameterizing the nuisance as the observation-scale amplitude B=A K(p)h^(2p-1) absorbs the apparent log(h) derivative. On the actual one-dimensional OU lattice this yields a conservative honest root-N profile interval, and an exact Gaussian KL calculation matches the rate. Exact-design affine stencil means and covariances plus numerical Bessel checks support the irregular d=2 route; affine annihilation removes its O(h) analytic bias and first-difference log-variance obstruction. Checks covered zero and sign-changing amplitudes, unidentifiable p, the two-scale failure, local and diverging amplitudes, exponent endpoints, boundary effects, unestimable ranges, and large variance constants; no complete current-literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform Gaussian profile calibration and mathematical attainment of the least-favorable quantile on the actual quasi-uniform designs across all local-amplitude and exponent-boundary sequences. A terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, is an explicit residual open question rather than a promised delivered object. EARLY KILL TEST: On adversarially perturbed d=2 quasi-uniform designs, certify a positive divided-difference separation constant for the exact affine-stencil moment curve, including coincident exponents, and verify the exact Bessel mean remainder is o(h); failure for every allowed fixed-radius construction forces a design/scope pivot. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_spatial_slope_infill_phase.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a finite-dimensional, root-N confidence set for the spatial slope beta that is uniformly honest over deterministic quasi-uniform designs, unknown cross-tail exponent p, and every sequence of signed cross-tail amplitudes A_N tending to zero, without exposure nugget noise?

source_refs.claim: Identifies the exposure effect when spatial confounding dissipates at local scales, but does not give uniform infill inference as the tail-separation amplitude vanishes.
source_refs.author: Yawen Guan, Garritt L. Page, Brian J. Reich, Massimo Ventrucci, and Shu Yang

source_refs.claim: Proves infill consistency of spatial GLS when the exposure contains nonspatial variation, while noting that misspecified analytic standard errors are not guaranteed valid.
source_refs.author: Brian Gilbert, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Abhirup Datta

source_refs.claim: Obtains root-n normality and closed-form variance estimation for double spatial regression, but leaves verifiable covariance conditions for spatially independent splitting unresolved.
source_refs.author: Nate Wiecha, Jane A. Hoppin, and Brian J. Reich

open_problems.why_unsolved: Available positive results obtain separation through nonspatial exposure variation, maintained local-unconfoundedness, or nuisance-learning conditions. In the no-nugget bivariate Matérn model, the identifying signal is instead a high-frequency cross-tail whose observation-scale amplitude can be local to zero; at A=0, p disappears from the observational law. This leaves a nuisance parameter unidentified on a boundary while actual fixed-domain observations remain strongly dependent, so pointwise CLTs and conventional plug-in profile quantiles do not establish uniform coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform Gaussian-experiment approximation for three or more affine-annihilating local moments, coupled to a feasible residual-scale studentized profile statistic with attainable critical values and a theorem giving 1-alpha coverage and O(N^(-1/2)) worst-case expected diameter uniformly over A_N, p, marginal nuisance parameters, and allowed designs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from unmeasured spatial confounding to scale-specific spectral separation and an environmental-health estimand.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unmeasured spatial confounding obstructs slope identification -> coherence may dissipate at local scales -> high-frequency separation can recover the slope -> inference must remain valid when that separation vanishes at the observation scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Express confounding bias through spectral coherence and identify the slope from local-scale dissipation of that coherence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed cross-tail restriction is a parametric, rate-explicit version of their local-scale identifying condition.

method_exemplars.technique: Filter a multivariate Gaussian field before smoothing its cross-periodogram, then prove relative consistency and asymptotic normality through covariance and cumulant control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required local-stencil slope moments are filtered cross-covariance statistics targeting the same high-frequency spectral matrix, but the proof must move from a lattice to the actual quasi-uniform design.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on a sufficient statistic for a functional nuisance parameter and calibrate a quasi-likelihood-ratio statistic uniformly without imposing identification strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At A=0 the exponent p is unidentified, so profile calibration must be robust to the same structural form of identification failure.

open_problems.open_problem: Can affine-annihilating local quadratic and cross-quadratic variations be given a joint root-N CLT with consistently estimable covariance on every bounded-degree deterministic quasi-uniform design in d=2, including boundary stencils and coincident cross-tail exponents?

source_refs.claim: Constructs consistent higher-order quadratic-variation estimators for Matérn microergodic parameters and smoothness on stratified, randomized, and deformed-lattice designs.
source_refs.author: Wei-Liem Loh, Saifei Sun, and Jun Wen

source_refs.claim: Proves root-n consistency and asymptotic normality for local inversion-free Matérn covariance estimation on multidimensional irregular lattices after preconditioning.
source_refs.author: Hossein Keshavarz, XuanLong Nguyen, and Clayton Scott

source_refs.claim: Shows quasi-uniform designs attain optimal Matérn kriging prediction rates, but studies prediction rather than local cross-moment CLTs or spatial-confounding slopes.
source_refs.author: Rui Tuo and Wenjia Wang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known irregular-design quadratic-variation results impose randomized, stratified, deformed-lattice, binning, or preconditioner structure. A general quasi-uniform point cloud has location-dependent stencil geometry, boundary effects at the raw local scale, and no Fourier diagonalization. For a bivariate field, cross-quadratic forms additionally require uniform covariance summability and separation of near-coincident power-law moment directions; scalar microergodic CLTs supply neither the needed separation constant nor the full covariance formula.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A design-uniform multivariate triangular-array CLT and covariance-consistency theorem for three or more exact affine stencils, with explicit bounds for boundary loss, denominator stability, aliasing, Bessel remainders, and the minimum divided-difference separation over p.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates local quadratic variation as the route from dense irregular observations to Matérn tail-parameter estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed-domain dependence defeats ordinary covariance-parameter arguments -> high-order local differences isolate rough spectral coefficients -> selected irregular designs permit consistent estimation -> arbitrary quasi-uniform d=2 designs require a joint cross-moment CLT.

method_exemplars.technique: Precondition dense Matérn observations locally, represent the estimator through sparse Gaussian quadratic forms, and prove root-n normality with trace and concentration bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Affine-annihilating stencil statistics are sparse preconditioned quadratic forms, but the desired proof must cover cross-forms and a larger deterministic design class.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose higher-order divided differences to cancel analytic covariance terms and isolate Matérn irregular coefficients on irregular sampling schemes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required affine annihilation and exponent separation are direct multiscale extensions of this quadratic-variation construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Control bias, covariance, and joint cumulants of filtered cross-spectral statistics under fixed-domain Gaussian sampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies multivariate cross-statistic CLT machinery absent from scalar irregular-design quadratic-variation papers.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax honest expected-length and squared-risk frontier for estimating beta across the vanishing-cross-tail submodels A_N=O(N^(-1/2)), A_N=o(N^(-1/2)), and A_N=0 when p and the Matérn ranges are nuisance parameters?

source_refs.claim: Uses equivalence of Gaussian measures to show that fixed-domain data cannot consistently separate scalar Matérn variance and range although a microergodic combination is estimable.
source_refs.author: Hao Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Proves n^{-1/2} Gaussian behavior for the Matérn microergodic parameter uniformly over a nuisance range, with known smoothness, and shows nonconcentration of a regression intercept in the one-dimensional OU case.
source_refs.author: Cheng Li

source_refs.claim: Makes local-scale decay of exposure-confounder coherence the key identifying condition, but does not quantify honest interval length as that decay becomes local to zero.
source_refs.author: Yawen Guan, Garritt L. Page, Brian J. Reich, Massimo Ventrucci, and Shu Yang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing microergodicity results determine which scalar covariance combinations are estimable, and existing LAN results concern those combinations under known smoothness. They do not construct least-favorable pairs that simultaneously perturb beta, the signed cross-tail amplitude, p, and nonmicroergodic ranges while preserving the bivariate spectral determinant. Thus the literature does not determine whether adaptation through A=0 is free, changes only constants, or becomes impossible at a particular local-amplitude scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rate-sharp Le Cam lower bound proving that the infimum worst-case expected confidence-set diameter is at least cN^(-1/2) and minimax squared risk is at least c'N^(-1), using explicit least-favorable Gaussian spectral alternatives valid in each local-amplitude regime and accompanied by a matching attainable procedure.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents fixed-domain Matérn inference as a nonregular problem governed by microergodicity and uniform LAN rather than ordinary independent-data asymptotics.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Dense sampling creates stronger dependence -> only microergodic combinations concentrate -> uniform LAN recovers root-n inference for those combinations -> determine the honest information bound for beta when its cross-tail nuisance vanishes.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct equivalent Gaussian measures by matching spectral tails and use orthogonality to locate the estimable combination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Least-favorable beta alternatives must exploit the same fixed-domain equivalence geometry for a bivariate spectral matrix.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish LAN for a microergodic parameter uniformly over a nonmicroergodic range nuisance and derive its Gaussian limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired KL expansion is a beta-and-cross-tail extension of this uniform fixed-domain LAN calculation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class moduli of continuity to derive expected-length lower bounds for honest adaptive confidence intervals and construct matching procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The vanishing-amplitude submodels form nested classes, so their between-class modulus directly organizes the honest adaptation cost.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the necessary and sufficient Gaussian-measure equivalence conditions, and hence the microergodic parameter map, for the observational pair (X,Y) when X and W have Matérn-one-half marginals and a signed cross-spectrum A(alpha_C^2+||omega||^2)^(-(p+d/2)), including A=0?

source_refs.claim: Shows that scalar Matérn variance and range are not separately consistently estimable in d<=3 and identifies their microergodic combination.
source_refs.author: Hao Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Constructs valid bivariate Matérn cross-covariances with positive or negative colocated correlation, but does not characterize fixed-domain equivalence classes or slope recoverability.
source_refs.author: Tilmann Gneiting, William Kleiber, and Martin Schlather
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Derives fixed-domain normality of filtered cross-periodograms for multivariate Gaussian lattice data without an equivalence classification for the bivariate Matérn regression law.
source_refs.author: Chae Young Lim and Michael L. Stein

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar Matérn equivalence theory compares one covariance spectrum, whereas this observed law has a 2-by-2 spectral matrix in which beta, marginal microergodic combinations, and the cross-tail coefficient interact. Matrix positive-definiteness permits either sign of A, and at A=0 the exponent p drops out. Existing multivariate Matérn work establishes covariance validity and flexibility, while cross-periodogram theory assumes a fixed high-frequency model rather than determining which complete parameter tuples induce equivalent measures.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if equivalence-or-orthogonality theorem for two parameter tuples on bounded domains in d=1,2, together with an explicit high-frequency recovery map for beta and the identifiable combinations of A, p, and marginal scale-range parameters.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames why flexible signed cross-dependence is needed before specifying a precise admissible multivariate Matérn family.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Multivariate spatial variables require valid cross-covariances -> Matérn marginals admit flexible signed dependence -> validity alone does not imply fixed-domain identifiability -> classify the observational equivalence classes and beta recovery map.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare spectral-density tails and apply equivalence-versus-orthogonality criteria for Gaussian measures to isolate the scalar Matérn microergodic combination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is the matrix-valued analogue with beta and a vanishing off-diagonal tail added to the equivalence calculation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use spectral-matrix positivity to derive admissible cross-covariance parameter restrictions for bivariate Matérn fields.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The determinant-margin assumption in the target model is the matrix-positivity condition required before equivalence can be analyzed.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate high-frequency cross-spectral coefficients with filtered cross-periodograms and prove their joint Gaussian limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the recovery map is known, their filtered multivariate spectral statistic is the nearest existing estimator-and-limit template.

open_problems.open_problem: Can basis-voting spatial-confounding estimators be equipped with uniformly valid confidence sets when the plurality margin weakens to zero and exposure-confounder separation is a continuous Matérn cross-tail rather than a finite set of exactly valid basis coordinates?

source_refs.claim: Proves consistency of a plurality-rule basis-voting slope estimator and candidate-level normality, but identifies valid inference for the aggregate mode estimator as a future direction.
source_refs.author: Anik Burman, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Abhirup Datta

source_refs.claim: Models exposure-confounder separation continuously through spectral coherence rather than through finitely many exactly valid basis functions.
source_refs.author: Yawen Guan, Garritt L. Page, Brian J. Reich, Massimo Ventrucci, and Shu Yang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The basis-voting aggregate is a nonsmooth mode of dependent candidate estimators. Its consistency proof assumes a fixed strict plurality gap, while a vanishing Matérn cross-tail can produce many nearly tied, weakly valid basis coordinates and make the plurality margin local to zero. The basis-voting and spectral-adjustment literatures do not supply a result combining weak-plurality asymptotics, continuous cross-tail separation, and honest inference for the aggregate mode.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A weak-plurality limit experiment and confidence-set construction for beta with uniform coverage over N-dependent plurality margins and Matérn cross-tail amplitudes, including a characterization of when the interval remains root-N and when it must widen.

writing_exemplar.why: It links a precise identification assumption to smooth environmental exposures and the county-level PM2.5/COVID application that is the intended conditional consumer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smooth exposures defeat rougher-exposure adjustment -> plurality of exposure-only basis directions restores identification -> basis voting estimates a homogeneous environmental-health slope -> valid inference is needed as plurality and tail separation become weak.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate differential basis support into a plurality condition and recover beta as the mode of candidate projection or drop-one slopes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination preserves their estimand and applied setup while replacing a fixed plurality gap with a vanishing spectral-tail margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests with uniform size when identification strength is unrestricted.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A weak plurality margin makes the identity of valid basis candidates weakly identified, requiring inference that does not condition on strong separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Neyman-orthogonal scores and cross-fitting to remove first-order nuisance-estimation error, then prove root-n normality with feasible variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the basis-voting profile can be locally regularized, orthogonalization is a plausible route for preventing estimated spatial basis coefficients from contaminating the slope limit law.

literature_map:
1. Paciorek (2010, Statistical Science, DOI 10.1214/10-STS326) made relative spatial scale central to confounding bias and precision.
2. Zhang (2004, JASA, DOI 10.1198/016214504000000241) established the scalar Matérn microergodic frontier under fixed-domain sampling.
3. Du, Zhang and Mandrekar (2009, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0909.0359) proved exact and tapered-MLE CLTs on a bounded line.
4. Kaufman and Shaby (2013, Biometrika, arXiv:1108.1851) showed joint range-variance estimation preserves microergodic asymptotics but can materially affect finite samples.
5. Gneiting, Kleiber and Schlather (2010, JASA, DOI 10.1198/jasa.2010.tm09420) supplied valid signed bivariate Matérn cross-covariance models, not their fixed-domain equivalence theory.
6. Lim and Stein (2008, JMVA, DOI 10.1016/j.jmva.2008.02.005) proved filtered cross-periodogram consistency and normality for multivariate Gaussian lattice data.
7. Loh, Sun and Wen (2021, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/21-AOS2077) estimated Matérn smoothness and microergodic parameters by higher-order variations on selected irregular designs.
8. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott (2019, EJS, arXiv:1811.12602) obtained root-n local inversion-free Matérn inference on irregular lattices through sparse preconditioning.
9. Li (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2010.02126) proved uniform LAN-like posterior behavior for a Matérn microergodic parameter over nuisance ranges, with smoothness fixed.
10. Tuo and Wang (2020, JMLR 21:187) established quasi-uniform-design optimality for Matérn kriging prediction, not cross-tail slope inference.
11. Guan et al. (2023, Biometrika, arXiv:2012.11767) identify spatial effects when confounding coherence dissipates locally, but do not study vanishing separation.
12. Gilbert, Ogburn and Datta (2025, Biometrika, arXiv:2308.12181) prove GLS consistency using nonspatial exposure variation and caution that analytic standard errors may be invalid.
13. Bolin and Wallin (2024, arXiv:2403.18961) show infill GLS coefficients can collapse to zero or diverge under smoothness misspecification, sharpening the need for tail-robust analysis.
14. Wiecha, Hoppin and Reich (2025, Biometrics, arXiv:2404.09358) deliver root-n double-spatial-regression inference but leave verifiable spatial-splitting conditions unresolved.
15. Burman, Ogburn and Datta (2025, arXiv:2510.22464) handle smooth exposures by basis plurality and apply it to PM2.5/COVID, while leaving valid aggregate-mode inference open.
